style.northStar: An original 1994-1997 arcade and DOS giant-Frame fighter with disciplined held-cel animation, mechanically coherent machines, expressive cel-painted Pilots, hard industrial broadcast UI, and readable spectacle.
productionLessons: three-part move staging: anticipation, contact, recovery
limited local material ramps and deliberate pixel clusters
pilot personality and Frame identity treated as equal selection layers
industrial machinery must expose service, cooling, load and recoil logic
super presentation uses short portrait cut-ins, palette events and separate effects rather than long modern cinematics
forbidden: copying any commercial character, logo, stage, move animation or screen composition
random skulls, flames, chains, wings or unreadable spikes
modern PBR gloss or baked bloom
random glowing seams or crawling micro-panel noise
floating weapons or armour without declared attachments
phase effects replacing the physical body
smooth tweened anatomy used instead of authored key poses
provider-generated final contact sheets or packed atlases

sharedStateLibrary.purpose: secondary mechanical settle without human breathing
current shared light hit, guard crush and KO stagger body pose
guard compression distinct from neutral guard
heavy/counter reaction distinct from light hit

superPresentationStandard.name: Overdrive portrait-cut-in standard
superPresentationStandard.goal: Deliver a high-value 1990s arcade punctuation without turning the match into a long modern cinematic.

universalSequence.name: confirm
universalSequence.visual: two-tick input confirmation; no asset changes combat timing

universalSequence.name: palette-hit
universalSequence.visual: one hard palette flash and controlled stage darkening

universalSequence.name: pilot-charge
universalSequence.visual: first portrait cel enters on a hard rail

universalSequence.name: pilot-call
universalSequence.visual: second portrait cel plus separately authored bitmap move name

universalSequence.name: pilot-resolve
universalSequence.visual: third portrait cel and Frame-specific screen field lock

universalSequence.name: body-release
universalSequence.visual: portrait clears before the real hero-contact body cel

universalSequence.name: impact
universalSequence.visual: body contact, hitstop, Frame FX and brief camera response

universalSequence.name: return
universalSequence.visual: stage palette and HUD restore immediately after the effect contract ends

rules: pilot cut-in may animate eyes and mouth across three held cels
cut-in is a framed strip or command card, not a full video
the opponent cannot be obscured for the whole active sequence
the physical Frame remains readable at the hero contact
all move names are separately authored bitmap text
all Frame effects are separate from body cells
runtime super freeze, hitstop and damage remain game-authoritative

presentationBudget.rule: Presentation ticks may occupy existing game-authoritative super-freeze windows but may never change combat startup, active, recovery, damage or hitstop.

postLaunchMoveBacklog.purpose: Record desirable fighter depth without pretending it is implemented or allocating final launch cels.

sharedCandidates.description: one Frame-specific forward normal that reinforces silhouette and spacing
one Frame-specific low or overhead utility normal
only if paired receiver choreography remains readable at 128x128
only after first Overdrive, reversal and CORE presentation are proven

postLaunchMoveBacklog.gate: requires a separately versioned move, hitbox, source-cell and runtime-atlas contract

files.authority: Frame-specific normal and reversal IDs, timing and hit levels
public move naming and production choreography

sourceReview.rule: Any different game revision or live slot-manifest hash requires a fresh source review before final promotion; newer revisions are not assumed compatible.
